Q: Page crashes whenever I link a CSS stylesheet on one file, but doesn't on another A:

The browser resolves href="style.css" relative to the document's base URL, which is the current location (unless you've defined a <base>). From the looks of your error message, it's possible that the style sheet request is matching a route that uses route parameters as input (e.g., to query a database), but it expects the route parameter to be an integer, not "style.css".

Changing your style sheet href to a root-relative path href="/style.css" will likely fix the issue.

Below are some examples of how the style sheet href and the current location affect endpoint resolution. Notice how a root-relative href removes variability caused by the location.

href Location path Endpoint
href="style.css" /foo GET /style.css
href="style.css" /foo/bar GET /foo/style.css
href="/style.css" /foo GET /style.css
href="/style.css" /foo/bar GET /style.css

You can verify this request path in the DevTools Network tab, and you can follow the style sheet request in your app with logs or a debugger.

Q: content area not found in my page with elementor A:

In my case, I had to deactivate the Atomic Editor features in Elementor > Settings.

I also tried saving permalinks, checking template errors, theme compatibilities and plugin conflicts but none of that helped.

Q: Log current index while traversing a multidimensional array A:

You missed to remove the array item created in the recursion:

With the array [1,2,3] (n=0), we get the values for index:

[0,0], [0,1], [0,2]

Now, for the second array [4,5,6] (n=1), we start with index equals [0,2].

The command

index[index.length-1] = n

changes the last position, wich has the value 2:

[0, 1]

To correct this, use the function pop() to remove the index created in the recursion (or use an auxiliar variable, as on the other answer):

index.pop()


let arr = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]

function traverseDeep(arr, index) {
    index.push(0)
    for (let n = 0; n < arr.length; n++) {
        index[index.length-1] = n
        if (Array.isArray(arr[n])) {
            traverseDeep(arr[n], index); // Recursively jump inside the nested array
            index.pop();
        } else {
            console.log('value: '+arr[n]+' index: ['+index+']')
        }
    }
}

traverseDeep(arr, [])

Q: Arrays in a POSIX compliant shell A:

You can use the argument list $@ as an array in POSIX shells

It's trivial to initialize, shift, unshift, and push:

# initialize $@ containing a string, a variable's value, and a glob's matches
set -- "item 1" "$variable" *.wav

# shift (remove first item, accepts a numeric argument to remove more)
shift

# unshift (prepend new first item)
set -- "new item" "$@"

# push (append new last item)
set -- "$@" "new item"

Here's a pop implementation:

# pop (remove last item, store it in $last)
i=0 len=$#
for last in "$@"; do 
  if [ $((i+=1)) = 1 ]; then set --; fi  # increment $i. first run: empty $@
  if [ $i = $len ]; then break; fi       # stop before processing the last item
  set -- "$@" "$last"                    # prepend (unshift) $last to $@
done
echo "$last has been removed from ($*)"

($* joins the contents of $@ with $IFS, which defaults to a space character.)

Iterate through the $@ array and modify some of its contents:

i=0
for a in "$@"; do 
  if [ $((i+=1)) = 1 ]; then set --; fi  # increment $i. first run: empty $@
  a="${a%.*}.mp3"       # example tweak to $a: change extension to .mp3
  set -- "$@" "$a"      # add $a back to $@
done

Refer to items in the $@ array:

echo "$1 is the first item"
echo "$# is the length of the array"
echo "all items in the array (properly quoted): $@"
echo "all items in the array (in a string): $*"
[ "$n" -ge 0 ] && eval "echo \"the ${n}th item in the array is \$$n\""

(eval is dangerous, so I've ensured $n is a number before running it)

There are a few ways to set $last to the final item of a list without popping it:
with a function:

last_item() { shift $(($# - 1)) 2>/dev/null && printf %s "$1"; }
last="$(last_item "$@")"

... or with an eval (safe since $# is always a number):

eval last="\$$#"

... or with a loop:

for last in "$@"; do true; done

⚠️ Warning: Functions have their own $@ arrays. You'll have to pass it to the function, like my_function "$@" if read-only or else set -- $(my_function "$@") if you want to manipulate $@ and don't expect spaces in item values.

If you need to handle spaces in item values, it becomes much more cumbersome:

# ensure my_function() returns each list item on its own line
i=1
my_function "$@" |while IFS= read line; do
  if [ $i = 1 ]; then unset i; set --; fi
  set -- "$@" "$line"
done

This still won't work with newlines in your items. You'd have to escape them to another character (but not null) and then escape them back later. See "Iterate through the $@ array and modify some of its contents" above. You can either iterate through the array in a for loop and then run the function, then modify the variables in a while IFS= read line loop, or just do it all in a for loop without a function.

Q: How to attach a PDF file on WhatsApp Web using Selenium? (Error: “The file you tried to add is not supported”) A:

WhatsApp Web blocks Selenium's automated file uploads. Use Playwright + whatsplay instead:

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path
from whatsplay import Client, LocalProfileAuth

async def main():
    client = Client(
        auth=LocalProfileAuth(Path.home() / "wa_session"),
        headless=False,
    )
    await client.start()
    await client.send_file("Group Name", "/path/to/file.pdf")
    await client.stop()

asyncio.run(main())

pip install whatsplay
python -m playwright install chromium

Scans QR once, session persists. PDFs, images, any file type work.
